answer.rationale: Rollback is prohibited by compliance (security patch), so memory_b1 doesn't apply. Failover (b2) and circuit breakers (b4) don't match the symptom — write-path p99 climbing under heavy settlement write load points to primary database saturation, not a regional or dependency failure. Provisioning headroom (b3) takes time to provision and absorbed a predicted surge, whereas we need relief in minutes. Routing read/report traffic to read replicas directly offloads the primary during peak write load, which memory_b5 indicates recovered transactional write latency the same day with no write loss. It is reversible, preserves the patched release, and risks no customer writes. I want to verify b5 before committing because it is the sole basis for this choice.
